title: I Learned Portuguese in 30 Days (Then Tested It on a Real Brazilian)
creator: Kenji Learns Languages
description:
30 days, zero to a 15-minute conversation with my friend Bia in São Paulo. Here's what worked and what didn't.

Sponsored by Babbel: get up to 55% off your subscription at https://babbel.com/kenji

Conversation group I joined: Thursday nights online
Podcast I listened to: search "português para iniciantes"

sentences.t: Thirty days ago I knew exactly two words of Portuguese, obrigado and caipirinha.
Today I'm going to try to have a fifteen-minute conversation with my friend Bia in São Paulo, entirely in Portuguese, no English allowed.
But before that, let me tell you how the month actually went, because it did not go to plan.
Week one, I was way too ambitious.
I made this spreadsheet with two hours of study a day, and I kept it up for exactly three days.
And honestly, what saved the whole challenge was Babble, who's sponsoring this video.
Babble is a language app with short lessons, about ten or fifteen minutes each, built around real conversations instead of random vocabulary lists.
So instead of learning the word for elephant on day one, you learn how to order a coffee and ask for directions.
The part I used the most was the speech recognition, where you say the phrase out loud and it tells you if your pronunciation is off.
For Brazilian Portuguese that is a lifesaver, because the nasal sounds are brutal.
They also have live classes with real teachers, if you want someone to correct you in real time.
Right now you can get up to fifty-five percent off a subscription at babble dot com slash kenji.
That's babble dot com slash kenji, and the link is below.
So, week two.
I cut it down to one short lesson every morning, plus twenty minutes of a Brazilian podcast on my walk.
I understood maybe ten percent of the podcast.
But by the end of the week it was more like twenty, and that felt huge.
Week three is when I started talking.
I found a conversation group that meets online on Thursdays, and I was terrified.
My first sentence was supposed to be, I am learning Portuguese, and instead I said, I am a Portuguese.
Everyone was very kind about it.
Week four, I mostly just talked, to anyone, about anything.
I narrated my cooking out loud, I left voice messages for Bia, I argued with the GPS.
Okay, it's time.
Bia's on the call, and from here on it's Portuguese only.
So that went better than I expected?
We talked about her job, my trip to Lisbon last year, and food, mostly food.
I lost the thread twice, once when she started talking about her landlord, and once when she used the word saudade and then tried to explain it.
Saudade is this feeling of missing something or someone, a kind of sweet sadness, and apparently there's no real English word for it.
But I never switched to English, which was the whole goal.
So my verdict after thirty days?
I can get by, I can make friends, and I can embarrass myself confidently in a second language.
I'm going to keep going for another two months and then try a trip to Brazil.
If you want to see that, subscribe, and tell me what language you're learning in the comments.
